For **review, sketches, and dialectic** tasks routed through `scripts/launch-review.sh --tool cursor` and `scripts/launch-review.sh --tool codex`, Codex and Cursor are now mechanically sandboxed at the CLI level (issue #1529): Codex review runs as `codex exec --sandbox read-only` and Cursor review runs as `cursor agent -p --trust --mode plan` (issue #1583 removed `--sandbox enabled`, which crashed hosts where the cursor-agent sandbox runtime is unavailable — the prior `codex exec --full-auto` (workspace-write) and `cursor agent -p --force --trust` (force-allow commands) postures are gone). `/design` plan-review voting uses `scripts/dispatch-plan-voters.sh`, which launches external voters through `scripts/run-external-agent.sh` directly but keeps the same read-only CLI posture (`codex exec --sandbox read-only` and `cursor agent -p --trust --mode plan`) and waits on wrapper sentinels before returning voter paths. The review launchers also provide a HARD CONSTRAINTS read-only preamble so the model reasons about its read-only role: Cursor prepends it to the prompt, while Codex writes it to a per-invocation `CODEX_HOME/config.toml` top-level `instructions` key outside both `$PWD` and the review output `--add-dir`. The plan-voter dispatcher includes a narrower do-not-modify voter prompt but does not publish launcher-owned dirty-tree sidecars; its primary mechanical controls are the external CLI read-only modes plus the monitored wrapper. For Codex, the CLI sandbox is the primary mitigation and the instructions preamble is its prompt-level reinforcement; for Cursor, read-only enforcement relies on `--mode plan` plus the prompt preamble plus the post-hoc `${OUTPUT}.dirty-tree` detector on review-launcher lanes (Cursor/Codex/Gemini parity). Mechanical guarantee depends on the upstream Codex / Cursor CLIs continuing to honor `--sandbox read-only` / `--mode plan` respectively; the launcher harnesses (`scripts/test-launch-review.sh`) and plan-voter dispatcher harness (`scripts/test-dispatch-plan-voters.sh`) pin the argv literally, and review-launcher dirty-tree sidecars catch post-run mutation if a future CLI release silently changes those flags' semantics. Note that this hardening applies only to the **review-launcher and plan-voter lanes** — the implementer launchers (`scripts/launch-codex-implement.sh`, `scripts/launch-cursor-implement.sh`, `scripts/launch-gemini-implement.sh`) intentionally retain workspace-write / `--trust` because the implementer's job is to edit the tree (see "Step 2 implementation" paragraph below). The Gemini reviewer call sites have been removed from `/review` and `/implement --quick`, so the "review/sketches/dialectic" trust framing applies to Gemini only if those call sites are re-enabled (see "Gemini reviewer delegation (dormant)" below); the only currently-active Gemini delegation is the `--coder=gemini` implementer slot described in this paragraph. `/design` adaptive sketch process counts are projected in [`docs/topology.md`](docs/topology.md#design.sketch.regular_slots): full sketch mode launches 4 external agents, quick/simple sketch mode launches 2, and the codebase-scan-confirmed trivial-doc path launches 0 external sketch agents and writes sentinel artifacts instead. The trust model for nonzero sketch modes is unchanged — same scripts, same prompt constraints. `/implement` Step 2 implementation without an explicit `--coder` first honors the `/design` `diff_lines < 30` carve-out, then falls through Codex → Cursor → Claude by availability; an explicit `--coder=codex` still runs Codex (`codex exec --full-auto`, `approval: never`, `sandbox: workspace-write`). The Codex implementer launcher (`scripts/launch-codex-implement.sh`) writes the static implementer agent preamble to a per-invocation `CODEX_HOME/config.toml` top-level `instructions` key, symlinks `~/.codex/auth.json` into that temporary home only when the file exists, and keeps the temporary home outside both `$PWD` and the dispatcher session tmpdir. The launcher passes two `--add-dir` flags to `codex exec`: (1) `--add-dir "$(dirname "$MANIFEST_PATH")"` so Codex's `workspace-write` sandbox can atomic-write `manifest.json` and `qa-pending.json` to the dispatcher-owned session tmpdir (outside `$PWD`, typically under `~/.cache/larch/sessions/...`); and (2) `--add-dir "$PWD"` to explicitly grant write access to the repo root — without this second grant the `workspace-write` sandbox denies writes to repo-root files (`Makefile`, `AGENTS.md`, etc.) and paths under `.claude/`, producing `sandbox-denied-required-root-files` bails. Together these widen Codex's writable surface to the repo root (and all paths beneath it) plus the entire session tmpdir. Operators should treat the session tmpdir as Codex-writable (transcripts, sidecars, dispatcher baseline / spawn / resume-count sentinels), but it does not contain Codex's temporary config or auth symlink (those live under `$CODEX_HOME_DIR`). Cursor (`--trust`) and Gemini (`--approval-mode yolo --skip-trust`) already permit writes to arbitrary absolute paths and require no analogous launcher flag. The operator can opt into Cursor (`cursor agent ... --workspace "$PWD"`) with `--coder=cursor`, Gemini (`gemini --prompt ... --approval-mode yolo --skip-trust --model "$GEMINI_MODEL"`, where `$GEMINI_MODEL` is passed as a single quoted argv token so an operator-controlled `LARCH_GEMINI_MODEL` / `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_GEMINI_MODEL` value cannot expand into additional `gemini` CLI flags via word-splitting) with `--coder=gemini`, or the main Claude agent's Edit/Write path with `--coder=claude`. Gemini's `yolo` mode auto-approves all tool calls including shell commands, and `--skip-trust` bypasses Gemini's per-workspace trust prompt. When `--coder=cursor` or `--coder=gemini` is requested but the tool is unhealthy or unavailable, the dispatcher falls back to the main-agent Edit/Write path (`STATUS=claude_fallback`), symmetric to passing `--coder=claude` directly. **Codex, Cursor, and Gemini do not commit** — Codex cannot write `.git/` under `workspace-write`, and Cursor/Gemini prompts forbid commits. Cursor and Gemini have full filesystem access, so the dispatcher (`skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh`) mechanically asserts `HEAD == BASELINE_SHA` before committing on their behalf and bails with `cursor-modified-history` or `gemini-modified-history` if the tool created or amended commits, preserving partial work for operator inspection. Operators who want a stricter sandbox model should prefer `--coder=codex`. The dispatcher pipes `manifest.commit_message` through `scripts/redact-secrets.sh`, writes the redacted output to a tmpfile, and runs `git add -A && git commit -F <tmpfile>` on the implementer's behalf — so what lands in git history is the manifest's `commit_message` modulo the redactor (the same scrubber used downstream for the canonical on-disk manifest). The redactor pass before `git commit` is load-bearing: without it, a secret accidentally embedded in `commit_message` would land permanently in git history while the on-disk canonical manifest's redacted copy would suggest the secret had been scrubbed (split brain). `git add -A` stages every working-tree change (tracked + untracked) — under this trust model the working tree IS the source of truth, `manifest.files_touched` is advisory documentation only (no diff cross-check), and operator review + `/review` (Step 5) + the regular pre-commit hook chain are the downstream backstops against external implementers committing files outside the declared scope. Operators concerned about scope drift should review the produced commit before allowing the merge. There is no Claude-side diff verification — the working tree IS the source of truth, and `commit_message` flows into `git commit -F` modulo the secrets-family redaction described above. External implementer process writes bypass the Edit/Write PreToolUse hook chain (including `block-submodule-edit.sh`); the regular `pre-commit` hook chain runs when the dispatcher commits, providing a second-line backstop. Post-implementer validation in `skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh` mechanically enforces, BEFORE the dispatcher commits: (1) `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` matches the spawn-time branch (→ `branch-changed`); (2) `git hash-object .claude-plugin/plugin.json` matches the spawn-time baseline, catching working-tree edits to the version-bump-reserved file (→ `protected-path-modified`); (3) `git submodule status --recursive` reports clean (→ `submodule-dirty`); (4) every manifest path is rejected if it contains `..`, starts with `/`, equals `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, or resolves under a submodule (→ `protected-path-modified`); (5) Cursor/Gemini only: `HEAD` still matches the spawn-time baseline (→ `cursor-modified-history` / `gemini-modified-history`). The earlier diff cross-check (`manifest-diff-mismatch`), commit-subject equality (`commit-subject-mismatch`), working-tree-clean (`dirty-tree-after-codex`), and commits-since-baseline (`no-commit-since-baseline`) checks were removed when commit responsibility moved off Codex — they were tautological under the new model, since the dispatcher itself produces the commit from `manifest.commit_message`. If `git commit` fails (empty working tree, pre-commit hook rejection, transient git error), the dispatcher emits `commit-failed`, removes the un-sanitized `manifest.json` from `$IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR` to avoid leaving raw text fields on disk, captures `git commit` stderr to `$IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR/<tool>-commit-stderr.txt`, and bails — the index stays fully staged from the prior `git add -A` (no new commit was produced) so operators may need `git reset` or `git commit --amend` after diagnosing the failure, not only inspection. Manifest text fields (`commit_message`, `summary_bullets[]`, `todos_left[]`, `oos_observations[*].title|description`) are run through `scripts/redact-secrets.sh` before any consumption by downstream Steps 4 / 8a / 9a / 9a.1, since they flow verbatim into commit messages, the CHANGELOG, the PR body, and public GitHub issues. Claude does NOT inspect implementer transcripts or run `git diff` to figure out what changed — only the validated, sanitized manifest is consumed downstream. For `/research` — which launches external agents directly against `$PWD` — the trust framing (mechanical PreToolUse hook on `/research`'s `Edit|Write|NotebookEdit` surface, prompt-only posture for Bash and external agents, residual risks, and scope of the mechanical guarantee) is documented in the [External reviewer write surface in /research](#external-reviewer-write-surface-in-research) subsection below.
34:**Claude review subprocesses**: `scripts/launch-claude-subprocess.sh` is used for `/review` Claude fallback slots and tie-breaker style tasks. It validates prompt, context, and output paths against containment roots (plugin root or the session tmpdir), rejects symlinks, rejects `..` and control characters, caps context to 20 files and 256 KB per file, and wraps context as untrusted input. It emits `.meta`, `.done`, and `.dirty-tree` sidecars so the collector can reason about the subprocess like an external reviewer. The default model is `claude-sonnet-4-6` and can be overridden with `--model`. Unlike Codex and Cursor review launchers, this wrapper has no mechanical read-only CLI sandbox; read-only behavior is prompt-level only and enforced post-hoc through dirty-tree sidecar aggregation.
54:**Gemini reviewer delegation (dormant)**: the Gemini reviewer call sites in `/review` and `/implement --quick` have been removed. The launcher (`scripts/launch-review.sh --tool gemini`) is also disabled by default at runtime: valid invocations exit 0 with an empty output file unless `GEMINI_REVIEW=1` is set. Its admin-policy file (`scripts/gemini-reviewer-policy.toml`), the regression harness (`scripts/test-launch-review.sh`), the Gemini health probe in `scripts/check-reviewers.sh`, and the `--check-gemini-reviewer` opt-in flag in `scripts/session-setup.sh` are retained as machinery so the lane can be re-enabled deliberately by setting the env gate and re-introducing call sites in those skills. The reviewer prompt is inlined at the call sites and is not a separate file. (`agents/gemini-implementer.md` is the system prompt for the **implementer** slot — `--coder=gemini` — and is unrelated to the dormant reviewer launcher.) The mechanical posture described below applies if those call sites are restored and `GEMINI_REVIEW=1` is set. The argv shape would be `gemini -m "$GEMINI_MODEL" -p "$PROMPT" -o json --skip-trust --approval-mode yolo --admin-policy "$SCRIPT_DIR/gemini-reviewer-policy.toml"` — `$GEMINI_MODEL` resolves from `LARCH_GEMINI_MODEL` then `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_GEMINI_MODEL`, defaulting to `gemini-2.5-pro` — wrapped by `scripts/launch-review.sh --tool gemini`. The plugin-shipped admin policy denies Gemini reviewer file-write tools (`write_file`, `replace`, `edit`, `edit_file`, `delete_file`) at admin priority 5999, while shell remains governed by `--approval-mode yolo` so reviewers can inspect `git diff`, `git log`, and repository files. Gemini is also available as `--coder=gemini` for the implementer slot (see External tool delegation above). The implementer launcher (`scripts/launch-gemini-implement.sh`) keeps the yolo + write-tools posture and remains separate from this read-only reviewer policy; implementer Gemini does not vote, and does not participate in design sketches or dialectic/research lanes. Note: the implementer launcher normalizes its preflight envelope on `resolve_gemini_model` failure (always emits `MANIFEST_WRITTEN=false` / `QA_PENDING_WRITTEN=false` so a stale manifest left by an earlier attempt cannot be misclassified as a completed run); this hardens the launcher's KV stdout grammar without changing its trust posture. Reviewer prompts ask Gemini to inspect the live repository directly and include explicit `Do NOT modify files. Do NOT commit. Do NOT push.` instructions, matching the prompt constraints used for Cursor's `--trust` reviewer lane and Codex's `--full-auto` reviewer lane; the launcher also prepends a stronger read-only preamble that bans shell redirects, `tee`, mutating filesystem commands, git/index/ref mutation, and write-capable tools. `--approval-mode yolo` auto-approves Gemini tool calls, including shell commands, and `--skip-trust` bypasses Gemini's trust prompt; the admin policy adds a file-write-tool deny rule for Gemini reviewer mode, but it is not a general filesystem sandbox and depends on stable Gemini tool names. The reviewer launcher therefore adds a repo-root snapshot guard: after stale launcher artifacts are removed and before Gemini launches, it records `HEAD` plus tracked and untracked file hashes, then compares after JSON normalization. Any repo mutation, including shell-redirect bypasses the policy cannot see, fails the lane with a loud diagnostic and reverts modified tracked files, deleted tracked files, and new untracked files to their pre-launch state where possible. The guard is fail-open outside git worktrees and bounded by `LARCH_GEMINI_SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT` (default 30s); those cases fall back to the policy-plus-prompt posture and emit diagnostics. Gemini-cli tool catalog drift is checked at health-probe time: unknown tool names emit a `GEMINI_TOOL_DRIFT_WARNING=` key that `session-setup.sh` re-emits as a banner, while unknown names whose tokenized form (camelCase / `_` / `-` / `.` boundaries) anchored-matches a write-style keyword, or fixture-known write-style tools missing from the deny list, mark Gemini unhealthy until the deny list or fixture is updated. The alarm covers the gemini-cli catalog discovered under the probe argv (`--approval-mode plan`); the reviewer runs under `--approval-mode yolo --admin-policy`, so probe-mode catalog drift is a proxy for, not a strict superset of, reviewer-mode catalog drift. This mechanical guarantee depends on gemini-cli continuing to honor `--admin-policy` from arbitrary file paths; gemini-cli's documentation describes admin-policy as "OS-specific system directories", so a future release that restricts the flag would degrade the launcher to prompt-only plus snapshot enforcement (the existing fail-closed path catches gemini-cli flag-parse failures). When Gemini is unavailable, unhealthy, times out, emits invalid JSON, or trips the snapshot guard, larch skips the Gemini lane for the remainder of the session instead of substituting Claude, preserving the strict additive contract. The launcher also emits a `${OUTPUT}.dirty-tree` sidecar (matching the Cursor/Codex contract introduced for `/review` Step 5 by #1437) so that, when the Gemini reviewer call sites are reintroduced, sidecar-only consultation picks up Gemini coverage automatically with the same `STATUS=clean|dirty|unknown` enum and the same recovery contract; this dirty-tree sidecar is additive to the repo-root snapshot guard described above.
58:**Retry-metadata deserialization (issue #1154)**: External-agent `.meta` sidecars store the child argv as a JSON array (`CMD_JSON`), validated as an `array` of `string` before deserialization. Retry launches use direct Bash array expansion; `eval` is no longer used to reconstruct argv from persisted shell-quoted text. Malformed or missing metadata fails closed: the original result is marked unhealthy and the tool is flipped to unhealthy for the rest of the session. `TIMEOUT=` is part of validated retry metadata. Missing, non-digit, or zero/zero-padded values fail closed for that reviewer (`mark_retry_metadata_invalid` + `set_tool_unhealthy`), aligning the reader-side contract with `scripts/run-external-agent.sh`'s writer-side validation. The legacy `CMD_JSON` branch also applies per-tool argv-shape allowlists: Cursor must look like `cursor agent ... --workspace ...` and cannot carry `--add-dir`; Codex must look like `codex exec ... -C ... --output-last-message ...`; Gemini must start as `launch-review.sh --tool gemini`, `launch-gemini-implement.sh`, or `gemini` and cannot carry Codex/Cursor workspace-widening flags. Unknown `TOOL=` values fail closed. `.done` sentinel content is also treated as tamperable data: the collector accepts only `^[0-9]{1,3}$` digit strings in the `0..255` range, otherwise stderr-logs and forces `EXIT_CODE=99`; `.done` files are per-session local artifacts under the session tmpdir and are not an authentication boundary. `.meta` files remain per-session local artifacts under the session tmpdir and are not an authentication boundary; the trust model treats them as data that may be tampered with by anything writing to that tmpdir.
60:**Cursor/Codex outer-launcher retry metadata and dirty-tree guard**: Cursor and Codex review retries may carry `OUTER_LAUNCHER`, `OUTER_LAUNCHER_PROMPT_FILE`, and `OUTER_LAUNCHER_WORKDIR` in the same `.meta` sidecar so retries replay through `scripts/launch-review.sh --tool cursor` or `scripts/launch-review.sh --tool codex` and keep launcher-owned post-processing. The collector treats these fields as tamperable data: all three must be present together, `OUTER_LAUNCHER` is rejected if it contains `..` and must canonicalize to the tool-matched allowlisted launcher, `OUTER_LAUNCHER_PROMPT_FILE` is pinned to `${ORIG_OUTPUT}.prompt` and must be a readable regular non-symlink file, and `OUTER_LAUNCHER_WORKDIR` is rejected on `..` and must be an existing directory. Invalid outer metadata fails closed instead of falling back to `CMD_JSON`, because replaying the inner command would skip launcher-owned post-processing and the mid-run dirty-tree guard. Each launcher captures a pre-launch untracked baseline and writes `${OUTPUT}.dirty-tree` before `${OUTPUT}.done`; `STATUS=dirty` or `STATUS=unknown` triggers automatic log-and-discard of the reviewer-introduced changes — no operator prompt is issued and no stash is created (see `skills/review/SKILL.md` Step 3a and `skills/implement/SKILL.md` Step 5.3.b). This guard detects reviewer writes after the fact; it does not prevent the reviewer process from writing during its run. `launch-cursor-implement.sh` writes analogous outer-launcher metadata for forward compatibility, but the collector does not allowlist it until an implement-side replay caller exists.
102:**`ship-pr.sh` post-review publication path**: `scripts/ship-pr.sh` centralizes `/implement`'s post-review PR publication, CI-fix, merge, and teardown mechanics. It preserves the existing public-output guards: PR bodies embed only sanitized Mermaid files or placeholders, `create-pr.sh` still redacts session tmpdir paths before `gh pr create`, and tracking issue lifecycle writes still route through `tracking-issue-write.sh`. The new CI-fix launchers (`launch-cursor-ci.sh`, `launch-codex-ci.sh`) invoke external tools through `run-external-agent.sh`, so their `.meta` sidecars inherit the same argv visibility tradeoffs documented for Cursor/Codex launchers.
116:2. **At-rest visibility in `.meta` `CMD_JSON` sidecars** — `scripts/run-external-agent.sh` records the full child argv into `${OUTPUT}.meta` as a `CMD_JSON=` line, because `scripts/collect-agent-results.sh` reconstructs retry argv from `CMD_JSON` on empty-output retries. Persisting `<redacted>` in `CMD_JSON` would silently break those retries by passing the literal `<redacted>` token to a relaunched Cursor child, so the larch design explicitly does NOT redact `CMD_JSON`. The `${OUTPUT}.meta` sidecars live under `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/larch/sessions/...` (session-tmpdir scoping; cleaned up by Step 18 of `/implement` and the parallel cleanup paths in `/design` / `/review` / `/research`). The session tmpdir is treated as session-scoped private state under existing `SECURITY.md` conventions; this PR does not change that posture.

The earlier diff cross-check (`manifest-diff-mismatch`), commit-subject equality (`commit-subject-mismatch`), working-tree-clean (`dirty-tree-after-codex`), and commits-since-baseline (`no-commit-since-baseline`) checks were removed when commit responsibility moved off Codex — they were tautological under the new model, since the dispatcher itself produces the commit from `manifest.commit_message`. Manifest text fields (`commit_message`, `summary_bullets[]`, `todos_left[]`, `oos_observations[*].title|description`) are run through `scripts/redact-secrets.sh` before any consumption by downstream Steps 4 / 8a / 9a / 9a.1, since they flow verbatim into commit messages, the CHANGELOG, the PR body, and public GitHub issues. Claude does NOT inspect implementer transcripts or run `git diff` to figure out what changed — only the validated, sanitized manifest is consumed downstream. For `/research` — which launches external agents directly against `$PWD` — the trust framing (mechanical PreToolUse hook on `/research`'s `Edit|Write|NotebookEdit` surface, prompt-only posture for Bash and external agents, residual risks, and scope of the mechanical guarantee) is documented in the [External reviewer write surface in /research](#external-reviewer-write-surface-in-research) subsection below.
34:**Claude review subprocesses**: `scripts/launch-claude-subprocess.sh` is used for `/review` Claude fallback slots and tie-breaker style tasks. It validates prompt, context, and output paths against containment roots (plugin root or the session tmpdir), rejects symlinks, rejects `..` and control characters, caps context to 20 files and 256 KB per file, and wraps context as untrusted input. It emits `.meta`, `.done`, and `.dirty-tree` sidecars so the collector can reason about the subprocess like an external reviewer. The default model is `claude-sonnet-4-6` and can be overridden with `--model`. Unlike Codex and Cursor review launchers, this wrapper has no mechanical read-only CLI sandbox; read-only behavior is prompt-level only and enforced post-hoc through dirty-tree sidecar aggregation.
54:**Gemini reviewer delegation (dormant)**: the Gemini reviewer call sites in `/review` and `/implement --quick` have been removed. The launcher (`scripts/launch-review.sh --tool gemini`) is also disabled by default at runtime: valid invocations exit 0 with an empty output file unless `GEMINI_REVIEW=1` is set. (`agents/gemini-implementer.md` is the system prompt for the **implementer** slot — `--coder=gemini` — and is unrelated to the dormant reviewer launcher.) The mechanical posture described below applies if those call sites are restored and `GEMINI_REVIEW=1` is set. The argv shape would be `gemini -m "$GEMINI_MODEL" -p "$PROMPT" -o json --skip-trust --approval-mode yolo --admin-policy "$SCRIPT_DIR/gemini-reviewer-policy.toml"` — `$GEMINI_MODEL` resolves from `LARCH_GEMINI_MODEL` then `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_GEMINI_MODEL`, defaulting to `gemini-2.5-pro` — wrapped by `scripts/launch-review.sh --tool gemini`. The plugin-shipped admin policy denies Gemini reviewer file-write tools (`write_file`, `replace`, `edit`, `edit_file`, `delete_file`) at admin priority 5999, while shell remains governed by `--approval-mode yolo` so reviewers can inspect `git diff`, `git log`, and repository files. Gemini is also available as `--coder=gemini` for the implementer slot (see External tool delegation above). The implementer launcher (`scripts/launch-gemini-implement.sh`) keeps the yolo + write-tools posture and remains separate from this read-only reviewer policy; implementer Gemini does not vote, and does not participate in design sketches or dialectic/research lanes. Note: the implementer launcher normalizes its preflight envelope on `resolve_gemini_model` failure (always emits `MANIFEST_WRITTEN=false` / `QA_PENDING_WRITTEN=false` so a stale manifest left by an earlier attempt cannot be misclassified as a completed run); this hardens the launcher's KV stdout grammar without changing its trust posture. Any repo mutation, including shell-redirect bypasses the policy cannot see, fails the lane with a loud diagnostic and reverts modified tracked files, deleted tracked files, and new untracked files to their pre-launch state where possible. The guard is fail-open outside git worktrees and bounded by `LARCH_GEMINI_SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT` (default 30s); those cases fall back to the policy-plus-prompt posture and emit diagnostics. Together these widen Codex's writable surface to the repo root (and all paths beneath it) plus the entire session tmpdir. Operators should treat the session tmpdir as Codex-writable (transcripts, sidecars, dispatcher baseline / spawn / resume-count sentinels), but it does not contain Codex's temporary config or auth symlink (those live under `$CODEX_HOME_DIR`). Cursor (`--trust`) and Gemini (`--approval-mode yolo --skip-trust`) already permit writes to arbitrary absolute paths and require no analogous launcher flag. The operator can opt into Cursor (`cursor agent ... --workspace "$PWD"`) with `--coder=cursor`, Gemini (`gemini --prompt ... --approval-mode yolo --skip-trust --model "$GEMINI_MODEL"`, where `$GEMINI_MODEL` is passed as a single quoted argv token so an operator-controlled `LARCH_GEMINI_MODEL` / `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_GEMINI_MODEL` value cannot expand into additional `gemini` CLI flags via word-splitting) with `--coder=gemini`, or the main Claude agent's Edit/Write path with `--coder=claude`. Gemini's `yolo` mode auto-approves all tool calls including shell commands, and `--skip-trust` bypasses Gemini's per-workspace trust prompt. When `--coder=cursor` or `--coder=gemini` is requested but the tool is unhealthy or unavailable, the dispatcher falls back to the main-agent Edit/Write path (`STATUS=claude_fallback`), symmetric to passing `--coder=claude` directly. **Codex, Cursor, and Gemini do not commit** — Codex cannot write `.git/` under `workspace-write`, and Cursor/Gemini prompts forbid commits. Cursor and Gemini have full filesystem access, so the dispatcher (`skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh`) mechanically asserts `HEAD == BASELINE_SHA` before committing on their behalf and bails with `cursor-modified-history` or `gemini-modified-history` if the tool created or amended commits, preserving partial work for operator inspection. Operators who want a stricter sandbox model should prefer `--coder=codex`. The dispatcher pipes `manifest.commit_message` through `scripts/redact-secrets.sh`, writes the redacted output to a tmpfile, and runs `git add -A && git commit -F <tmpfile>` on the implementer's behalf — so what lands in git history is the manifest's `commit_message` modulo the redactor (the same scrubber used downstream for the canonical on-disk manifest). The redactor pass before `git commit` is load-bearing: without it, a secret accidentally embedded in `commit_message` would land permanently in git history while the on-disk canonical manifest's redacted copy would suggest the secret had been scrubbed (split brain). `git add -A` stages every working-tree change (tracked + untracked) — under this trust model the working tree IS the source of truth, `manifest.files_touched` is advisory documentation only (no diff cross-check), and operator review + `/review` (Step 5) + the regular pre-commit hook chain are the downstream backstops against external implementers committing files outside the declared scope. Operators concerned about scope drift should review the produced commit before allowing the merge. There is no Claude-side diff verification — the working tree IS the source of truth, and `commit_message` flows into `git commit -F` modulo the secrets-family redaction described above. External implementer process writes bypass the Edit/Write PreToolUse hook chain (including `block-submodule-edit.sh`); the regular `pre-commit` hook chain runs when the dispatcher commits, providing a second-line backstop. Post-implementer validation in `skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh` mechanically enforces, BEFORE the dispatcher commits: (1) `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` matches the spawn-time branch (→ `branch-changed`); (2) `git hash-object .claude-plugin/plugin.json` matches the spawn-time baseline, catching working-tree edits to the version-bump-reserved file (→ `protected-path-modified`); (3) `git submodule status --recursive` reports clean (→ `submodule-dirty`); (4) every manifest path is rejected if it contains `..`, starts with `/`, equals `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, or resolves under a submodule (→ `protected-path-modified`); (5) Cursor/Gemini only: `HEAD` still matches the spawn-time baseline (→ `cursor-modified-history` / `gemini-modified-history`). The earlier diff cross-check (`manifest-diff-mismatch`), commit-subject equality (`commit-subject-mismatch`), working-tree-clean (`dirty-tree-after-codex`), and commits-since-baseline (`no-commit-since-baseline`) checks were removed when commit responsibility moved off Codex — they were tautological under the new model, since the dispatcher itself produces the commit from `manifest.commit_message`. Manifest text fields (`commit_message`, `summary_bullets[]`, `todos_left[]`, `oos_observations[*].title|description`) are run through `scripts/redact-secrets.sh` before any consumption by downstream Steps 4 / 8a / 9a / 9a.1, since they flow verbatim into commit messages, the CHANGELOG, the PR body, and public GitHub issues. Claude does NOT inspect implementer transcripts or run `git diff` to figure out what changed — only the validated, sanitized manifest is consumed downstream. For `/research` — which launches external agents directly against `$PWD` — the trust framing (mechanical PreToolUse hook on `/research`'s `Edit|Write|NotebookEdit` surface, prompt-only posture for Bash and external agents, residual risks, and scope of the mechanical guarantee) is documented in the [External reviewer write surface in /research](#external-reviewer-write-surface-in-research) subsection below.

-**Claude review subprocesses**: `scripts/launch-claude-subprocess.sh` is used for `/review` Claude fallback slots and tie-breaker style tasks. It validates prompt, context, and output paths against containment roots (plugin root or the session tmpdir), rejects symlinks, rejects `..` and control characters, caps context to 20 files and 256 KB per file, and wraps context as untrusted input. It emits `.meta`, `.done`, and `.dirty-tree` sidecars so the collector can reason about the subprocess like an external reviewer. The default model is `claude-sonnet-4-6` and can be overridden with `--model`. Unlike Codex and Cursor review launchers, this wrapper has no mechanical read-only CLI sandbox; read-only behavior is prompt-level only and enforced post-hoc through dirty-tree sidecar aggregation.

The sidecar is removed in the EXIT trap under normal operation. PID reuse is possible if the sidecar outlives the process (e.g. SIGKILL without cleanup); this is best-effort subprocess termination, not a hard security boundary. The default model is `claude-sonnet-4-6` and can be overridden with `--model`. Unlike Codex and Cursor review launchers, this wrapper has no mechanical read-only CLI sandbox; read-only behavior is prompt-level only and enforced post-hoc through dirty-tree sidecar aggregation.
